issues.detail: The Hebrew 'וְהוֹדַעְתִּי אֶת חֻקֵּי הָאֱלֹהִים וְאֶת תּוֹרֹתָיו' means 'and I will make known the statutes of God and His laws' — the statutes and laws belong to God (אֱלֹהִים). The Chinese renders '神的律法和我的律例' ('God's laws and my statutes'), incorrectly attributing the statutes (חֻקֵּי) to the speaker ('my') instead of to God. This changes the ownership of the statutes.
